subject.title: fix(security): bound hashFileContentsSync in approval script operand reads

question: Should approval-file fingerprinting become asynchronous through the approval-plan flow, or should OpenClaw intentionally enforce a documented finite operand-size policy for approval-bound scripts?
rationale: The patch cannot both preserve arbitrary-size script approval and bound synchronous wall-clock work; choosing the permanent compatibility and API behavior requires owner intent.

options.title: Make fingerprinting asynchronous
options.body: Propagate an asynchronous fingerprint step through the approval-plan path so large regular script operands retain approval support without blocking the event loop.

options.title: Adopt a finite approval-file policy
options.body: Reject or require a separate approval path for operands above an explicitly documented size limit, with compatibility and upgrade proof for existing workflows.

options.title: Pause this patch
options.body: Do not merge the partial mitigation until the approval-path owner selects and validates one of the durable policies.

recommendation.title: Make fingerprinting asynchronous
recommendation.body: Propagate an asynchronous fingerprint step through the approval-plan path so large regular script operands retain approval support without blocking the event loop.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available low-confidence routing signal from recent approval-denial work; a node-host code owner should confirm the final direction.
